issues.parameter: WD mass, radius and temperature model branch
issues.competing_evidence: Pala+22 reanalyzes the Gänsicke+06 HST UV data with Gaia EDR3 and reports 0.63 (+0.10/-0.08) Msun, R=0.013 (+0.0017/-0.0014) Rsun, and 19,248 (+486/-450) K; the original fit using Thorstensen d=79 (+8/-6) pc reported 0.78 (+0.12/-0.17) Msun, 7.61 (+1.6/-1.0)e8 cm, and 19,800 +/-700 K. Both depend on atmosphere fits and a WD mass-radius relation; neither is dynamical.
issues.why_it_matters: These values affect comparisons of WD masses and thermal states across magnetic and non-magnetic CVs.
issues.needed_action: Keep both fit branches in source comparisons; verify whether the intended community-facing default should be the Gaia-rescaled Pala+22 solution, and preserve the non-dynamical/model label.

issues.competing_evidence: Young+81 directly identifies 13 MG Zeeman absorption from an accreting polar-cap region; Wickramasinghe & Martin+85 find a poor-viewing-geometry centered-dipole fit near 22 MG and a better offset-dipole active pole near 14 MG; Bailey+91 IR cyclotron fit gives 14.5 +/-0.3 MG; Campbell+08 low-state IR cyclotron model gives 13.6 (+1.0/-0.8) MG with non-1sigma fit ranges.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating a polar-cap Zeeman value, global field geometry and cyclotron-column fields as one WD surface field would bias population comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep the distinct measurements and models separate; if a single field summary is required, choose which component and field geometry it represents. Do not average these values.

issues.parameter: Donor mass ratio and binary inclination
issues.competing_evidence: Southwell+95 reports irradiation-affected K2=198 +/-3 km/s, v sin i=92 +/-9 km/s, and uncorrected q=M2/M1=0.47 +/-0.08 as a lower estimate; corrected solutions are not unique. Davey & Smith+96 prefer i=45-60 deg using assumed q=0.6 and M2=0.26 Msun. Mason+24 obtains i=50.2 +/-2.0 deg from a low-state TESS/Wilson-Devinney model. Mason Table 1 sequence predicts M2=0.20 and R2=0.289 Rsun, but Table 2 reverses these and its prose uses M2=0.289 Msun.
issues.why_it_matters: Mass ratio and inclination control inferred component masses, donor evolutionary state and Roche geometry.
issues.needed_action: Verify the original Southwell correction and Mason+24 Table 1/Table 2/prose donor-value inconsistency before adopting a unique donor mass or a q-based component mass. Retain the inclination methods separately.

issues.parameter: X-ray flux band, absorption convention, epoch and state
issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 3 quotes 1.1 +/-0.1e-10 erg cm-2 s-1 in 1-10 keV from 4XMM-DR11-derived catalog bands and applies a 10% error floor. It does not give an AM Her 0.1-10 keV counterpart value; the underlying exact 4XMM detection ID, native flux row and absorption convention have not been matched here. ROSAT/4XMM soft-band flux varies substantially between epochs.
issues.why_it_matters: An assumed absorption correction or accretion state can change X-ray luminosity and radio/X-ray comparisons by large factors.
issues.needed_action: Query the exact 4XMM-DR11 detection(s) within the published source region; inspect native 0.2-12 keV Flux8, observation date, variability flags and any AM Her source-specific spectral fit. Do not label Ridder's converted value unabsorbed meanwhile.

issues.competing_evidence: Young+81 classifies the visible low-state donor spectrum as M4.5 V; Bailey+91 fits a 3250-K M-dwarf atmosphere template; Mason+24 repeats T2=3290 +/-70 K from Gänsicke+01. Southwell+95 finds phase-dependent weakening of Na I and cannot determine an unbiased subtype; these temperatures are template/secondary-reported values, not a direct irradiation-independent donor Teff.
issues.why_it_matters: Donor temperature and spectral type support donor-sequence/evolution comparisons, but irradiation and spectral templates can shift the inferred subtype.
issues.needed_action: Retrieve and inspect the cited Gänsicke+01 donor analysis if a direct donor temperature is needed; otherwise preserve all values as spectral/template or secondary-reported estimates.
